description: The approved-difference cases that are not rows of the precedence table and are not served-document metadata. Despite the file name these cover both the partition operation and the collection-side differences the precedence table does not reach: change-query scoping, the retained traditional messages, the omitted-limit default boundary, sizing in both its supplied-count and omitted-count forms, the header gating, the identity bound, and the full decoder matrix.

cases.note: Twenty-six documents against a host whose runtime maximum page size is well above twenty-five, with both limit and pageSize omitted. DMS applies its configured maximum, so the whole seed is returned. The published Ed-Fi default is 25, which stops one short: the seed is deliberately one document past that boundary, so a regression to the published default is detected rather than merely a test override being honored.

Twenty-five candidates over two requested partitions: a true ceiling sizes the partition at 13, so the second starts at candidate row 14. ODS spells the size as CEILING over two integer operands, so its CEILING receives an already-truncated quotient of 12 and its second partition starts at row 13, absorbing the surplus into a wider final range.

ODS's PartitionsController takes [FromQuery] int? number and then binds the same request against the generated {Resource}GetByExample with an empty prefix, so a case-insensitive match carries the same value into the filter specification and into the partition count. DMS removes the partition control from filter matching before the query-field lookup runs and answers with one meaning.

errors: The page token provided was invalid.

cases.note: The token names a range whose bounds exceed Int32, which DMS accepts and answers with an empty page because no document has an identity that high. ODS paging bounds are Int32 AggregateId values, so parsing the same payload fails and it answers with its invalid-token message.

The document identity sequence is reseeded so a single created document lands on Int64.MaxValue. DMS omits the header because advancing past that value would overflow. ODS gates its header on hydrated body count, so a non-empty body still carries one.

The rows are removed at the hydration boundary by a test-only decorator after real page selection produced a real non-null selected maximum; the header rule that answers is production code. ODS gates the header on hydrated body count, so an empty body ends its walk.
ODS 7.3.2's partitions controller carries no assigned-profile-usage enforcement filter, unlike its data-management controller base.

The omitted-count half of the same bullet. One hundred and five candidates against a configured default partition count of ten: a true ceiling sizes the partition at eleven and hands out exactly ten tokens, which is the at-most-the-default promise. ODS spells the size as CEILING over two integer operands, so its CEILING receives an already-truncated quotient of ten, and with number omitted both of its cap expressions read the nullable request value so no cap applies, leaving eleven starting ids and one token more than its configured default.

cases.note: The canonical form the encoder emits carries no padding. The approved decoder accepts it, while ODS decodes its standard-base64 token with an API that requires padding and rejects the same text. The page is empty because the seed is below the range the token names.
The same token with its padding restored. The approved decoder accepts either form, and a padded token is the form ODS itself emits.

cases.note: A payload carrying four comma-separated fields. The approved grammar is a fixed three-field form of an ordering marker and two bounds, and the ODS grammar is a fixed two-field form of two bounds, so both reject on field count.

errors: The page token provided was invalid.

cases.note: ODS parses its bounds with the framework's default integer styles, which allow a leading sign, so this two-field payload is accepted there. The approved grammar rejects it: it carries an ordering marker ahead of both bounds, so a two-field payload fails on field count before its decimal grammar — which accepts an optional leading minus and digits only — is reached. The payload stays two-field because a marked one would be rejected by ODS on field count and this case would stop being a difference.

errors: The page token provided was invalid.

cases.note: ODS's default integer styles allow leading and trailing white space, so this two-field payload parses there. The approved grammar rejects it: it carries an ordering marker ahead of both bounds, so a two-field payload fails on field count before its decimal grammar — which rejects whitespace inside a bound — is reached. The payload stays two-field for the same reason as the leading-sign case.
